title: Optimize 1.3 release notes (RC) — Performance Profiles & Cost Telemetry
body:
> **Archived 2026-02-18:** this page is superseded by "Optimize 1.3 release notes — Performance Profiles & Cost Telemetry" and is kept for reference only.

Summary
-------
Release notes for the Redwood Optimize 1.3 release candidate (1.3.0-rc1). Optimize 1.3 adds Performance Profiles, a telemetry-based Cost Estimator, latency-tier presets in the Console and a set of SDK/CLI usability fixes. It is aimed at customers tuning Dedicated and Hosted inference with Optimize who want predictable unit economics and an easier path to rolling out quantization/batching recommendations.

Highlights
----------
- Performance Profiles (feature flag: optimize.performance_profiles): per-model, per-workload profiles capturing measured latency, throughput and cost across sequence-length distributions. They feed auto-suggestion rules and the cost estimator.
- Telemetry-based Cost Estimator: uses historical request-shape telemetry (prefix length, tokens per request, hit rates) to project monthly cost with sensitivity analysis.
- Console latency-tier presets: S0: <50ms p95, S1: <150ms p95, S2: <250ms p95, each tuning batching and cache TTL recommendations.
- SDK v0.18.0: Optimize client with async estimate_cost() and get_performance_profile(); estimate() is renamed to estimate_cost() (breaking).
- CLI: redwood optimize export-profile <model> writes a reproducible YAML profile for Dedicated scheduling.
- Compatibility: default quantization profiles unchanged; optimize.legacy_hint is being removed (see Migration notes).

What's new (detailed)
---------------------
1) Performance Profiles
   - Captures distributions of sequence_length, tokens_generated, request_rate (qps) and prefix_cache_hit_rate, with p50/p95 latency and per-token GPU time per bucket (short/medium/long).
   - Stored versioned in the customer namespace (s3-backed); visible in Console and API.
   - API preview: POST /v1/optimize/profiles {"model":"redwood-7b-v1","workload":"chat-short"} returns a profile id plus recommendations.
   - Owner: Optimize team (Deepa Nair).

2) Telemetry-based Cost Estimator
   - Inputs: time window (default 14d), model(s), deployment mode (hosted/dedicated), commitment tier, sequence-length histogram.
   - Output: monthly projection (USD), token breakdown (input/system/output) and a sensitivity table for +10/25/50% tokens per request.
   - Caveats: accounts for measured batching efficiency and prefix cache hit rate; sparse or cold telemetry falls back to conservative defaults.
   - Console: "Cost Projection" panel with CSV download.

3) Latency-tier Presets
   - S0 (ultra-low latency), S1 (balanced), S2 (cost-efficient), each mapping to batching window targets, max batch size and prefix_cache_TTL suggestions.
   - Applied as heuristics over Performance Profiles; route-level policy can override.

4) SDK & CLI changes
   - SDK v0.18.0: estimate() -> estimate_cost(), async wrapper, structured CostEstimate return type.
   - CLI export-profile produces YAML for the Dedicated scheduler, e.g. redwood optimize export-profile redwood-13b-v2 --window 7d --out profile.yaml

Migration notes and breaking changes
----------------------------------
- optimize.legacy_hint (heuristic-only recommendations) is being removed; strip it from saved route configs. Once enforced, API calls including it return 400.
- SDK: replace estimate() with estimate_cost().
- Profile format v1 -> v2 adds "prefix_cache_hit_rate" buckets. The Dedicated scheduler accepts both; v1 is converted on import with a best-effort fill. Re-export after conversion.

Configuration snippets and examples
----------------------------------
- Console: Admin -> Optimize feature flags -> optimize.performance_profiles (default off for existing tenants, on for new tenants).

- Example API request (cost estimate):
  POST /v1/optimize/estimate_cost
  Content-Type: application/json

  {
    "model": "redwood-13b-v2",
    "deployment_mode": "dedicated",
    "window_days": 14,
    "sequence_histogram": {"short": 0.7, "medium": 0.25, "long": 0.05},
    "commitment_tier": "std-monthly-1"
  }

  Response (truncated):
  {
    "monthly_cost_usd": 11420.10,
    "cost_per_1k_output_tokens": 2.85,
    "sensitivity": {"+10%_tokens_per_request": 12562.11}
  }

- SDK migration (Python):
  # before
  cost = optimize_client.estimate(model="redwood-7b-v1", window_days=14)
  # after
  cost = await optimize_client.estimate_cost(model="redwood-7b-v1", window_days=14)

Rollout plan
------------
- Canary: 2026-02-10 -> enable Performance Profiles for 5 pilot tenants (medium-sized Dedicated customers with varied request shapes). Watch p95 latency impact and Console correctness.
- Gradual rollout: 2026-02-17 -> new tenants by default; existing tenants opt in via Console.
- Full enforcement of legacy_hint removal: date to be announced with GA.

SLOs and observability
----------------------
- Optimize API availability SLO unchanged at 99.9%.
- Cost estimator: 99% of estimates within 3s when Performance Profiles are cached; 95% within 5s otherwise.
- Metrics: optimize.profile_generation.count, optimize.estimate_latency_ms.p95, optimize.estimate_cache_hit_rate. Dashboard: /dashboards/optimize/1-3-release-estimates

How to opt-in
-------------
1) Console: Admin -> Feature flags -> optimize.performance_profiles -> "Enable" and accept data-sharing for profile generation.
2) API: POST /v1/optimize/profiles?action=generate with model + window_days.
3) CLI: redwood optimize export-profile --generate redwood-7b-v1 --window 7d --out my-profile.yaml

Owner and support
-----------------
- Product owner: Deepa Nair (Optimize)
- Engineering lead: Samir Gupta (Optimize infra)
- Support: support@redwood.ai (tag: optimize-1.3)
- Runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/optimize-profile-generation-runbook

Known issues and limitations
---------------------------
- Cold telemetry yields conservative projections (flagged in UI).
- Profile-merge race can produce duplicate buckets; fix targeted before GA.
- Dedicated accounts with strict region restrictions may hit S3 path policy errors on profile import; use CLI export/import via local file.

Changelog (selected)
--------------------
- 1.3.0-rc1 (2026-02-09): Release candidate. Performance Profiles, Cost Estimator, Console presets, SDK 0.18.0, CLI export-profile.

Appendix: reproducible profile YAML example
-----------------------------------------
name: redwood-13b-v2-chat-short
version: 2
model: redwood-13b-v2
workload: chat-short
buckets:
  - name: short
    pct: 70
    p95_latency_ms: 42
    tokens_per_request: 28
  - name: medium
    pct: 25
    p95_latency_ms: 120
    tokens_per_request: 160
  - name: long
    pct: 5
    p95_latency_ms: 420
    tokens_per_request: 1024
prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.34
recommendations:
  batching: {max_batch_size: 128, target_window_ms: 8}
  quantization: {profile: qc-2-8bit, expected_cpu_savings_pct: 18}

For migration help or a custom projection, contact Deepa or open a support ticket (tag: optimize-1.3).
